question: If a riding group grows larger than four or five riders, the handbook recommends:
choice_a: Riding two abreast to shorten the overall group length
choice_b: Dividing into two or more smaller groups
choice_c: Adding more group leaders at the front of the same group
choice_d: Increasing speed to reduce the group's total length
explanation: If your group is larger than four or five riders, divide it up into two or more smaller groups; small groups are easier and safer for other drivers to get around.
source_note: NC DMV Motorcyclists' Handbook (13th Ed., Sept. 2007), p.36, 'Keep the Group Small'

question: In a group ride, the handbook advises that inexperienced riders should be positioned:
choice_a: At the very back of the group
choice_c: Just behind the leader, so more experienced riders can watch them from the back
explanation: Put beginners up front, just behind the leader, so the more experienced riders can watch them from the back.
source_note: NC DMV Motorcyclists' Handbook (13th Ed., Sept. 2007), p.36, 'Keep the Group Together'

question: According to the handbook, a group's riding pace should generally be set by:
choice_a: Whichever rider wants to go the fastest
choice_b: The leader alone, regardless of who falls behind
choice_c: A predetermined fixed speed that never changes
choice_d: The tailender, with the group slowing if that rider falls behind
explanation: Follow those behind -- let the tailender set the pace, and if a rider falls behind, everyone should slow down a little to stay with the tailender.
source_note: NC DMV Motorcyclists' Handbook (13th Ed., Sept. 2007), p.36, 'Keep the Group Together'

question: Why does the handbook recommend that everyone in a group know the planned route?
choice_a: So a separated rider won't feel rushed to catch up or risk getting lost
choice_b: So individual riders can take independent shortcuts
choice_c: It is a legal requirement for any group ride
choice_d: So the fastest rider can choose a different route
explanation: Make sure everyone knows the route -- if someone is separated they won't have to hurry to keep from getting lost or taking a wrong turn.
source_note: NC DMV Motorcyclists' Handbook (13th Ed., Sept. 2007), p.36, 'Keep the Group Together'

question: The handbook advises against "pairing up" -- riding directly alongside another rider -- because:
choice_a: It is against the law in every state
choice_b: There is no place to go if you need to avoid a car or hazard
choice_c: It uses more fuel than staggered riding
choice_d: It makes hand signals impossible for others to see
explanation: Don't pair up -- never operate directly alongside another rider, since there is no place to go if you have to avoid a car or something on the road.
source_note: NC DMV Motorcyclists' Handbook (13th Ed., Sept. 2007), p.36, 'Keep Your Distance'

question: In a staggered formation, where does the leader typically ride within the lane?
choice_a: The right side of the lane
choice_c: The left side of the lane
explanation: In staggered formation, the leader rides in the left side of the lane, while the second rider stays one second behind in the right side of the lane.
source_note: NC DMV Motorcyclists' Handbook (13th Ed., Sept. 2007), p.36, 'Keep Your Distance'

question: In staggered formation, where does the second rider typically ride relative to the leader?
choice_b: Two seconds ahead of the leader
choice_c: In the center of the lane, level with the leader
choice_d: One second behind the leader, on the right side of the lane
explanation: The second rider stays one second behind the leader, positioned on the right side of the lane.
source_note: NC DMV Motorcyclists' Handbook (13th Ed., Sept. 2007), p.36, 'Keep Your Distance'

question: When passing in a staggered formation, the handbook says riders should pass:
choice_b: Two at a time, side by side
choice_c: All at once, as a full group
choice_d: Only when the entire group can pass in a single maneuver
explanation: Riders in a staggered formation should pass one at a time.
source_note: NC DMV Motorcyclists' Handbook (13th Ed., Sept. 2007), p.37, 'Keep Your Distance'

question: After the lead rider passes a vehicle in a group formation, the handbook says the leader should:
choice_a: Move to the right side of the lane to make room
choice_b: Return to the left position and continue at passing speed to open room for the next rider
choice_c: Slow down immediately back to the group's original speed
choice_d: Wait in the oncoming lane until the whole group has passed
explanation: After passing, the leader should return to the left position and continue riding at passing speed to open room for the next rider.
source_note: NC DMV Motorcyclists' Handbook (13th Ed., Sept. 2007), p.37, 'Keep Your Distance'

question: According to the handbook, when is single-file formation recommended for a group?
choice_a: At all times, regardless of road conditions
choice_c: When riding curves, turning, or entering or leaving a highway
choice_d: Only when the group has more than ten riders
explanation: It is best to move into a single-file formation when riding curves, turning, or entering or leaving a highway.
source_note: NC DMV Motorcyclists' Handbook (13th Ed., Sept. 2007), p.37, 'Keep Your Distance'
